patients.summary: Healthy elementary school teacher who joined in 2024. In July 2025 she survived a severe crash in which a friend was killed and developed an acute stress reaction managed by outside psychiatry and therapy, with one ED visit in January 2026 and no medication.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 26 y/o teacher looking to establish primary care with us. Has not had a local doctor; last seen at her old practice in 2023. Membership terms and fee reviewed, she enrolled over the phone. Insurance: employer PPO, card info entered. New patient physical scheduled 9/10 at 8:00 so she can come before school. Records release form emailed for her prior PCP.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26F here to establish. Teaches second grade, first week of the new school year went fine. Feels well, no complaints today.

PMH: none. No hospitalizations, no surgeries.
Meds: none, no supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother - hypothyroidism. Father - hypertension. No early heart disease, no cancers she knows of.
SH: single, lives alone. Never a smoker, does not drink at all, no recreational drugs. Walks most evenings, likes to hike on weekends.
GYN: regular cycles. Last Pap was at her old office, thinks 2023, told it was fine. Not currently sexually active.
Psych: no history of depression, anxiety or counseling. PHQ-2 0.

ROS: negative in full.

Exam: vitals as charted, BMI about 22. Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable, TMs clear. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged, no nodes. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear throughout. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin without concerning lesions. Neuro grossly intact. Mood and affect bright.

A/P: healthy adult, establishing care.
- Baseline labs today: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH (mom's thyroid history), one-time HIV and hep C screening.
- Records release signed; will pull her prior Pap and vaccine history before deciding what is due.
- Flu and updated COVID vaccine once the fall supply is in; nurse visit next month.
- Return in a year for her physical, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sadie, all of your labs came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, and thyroid. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative, so those never need repeating unless your risk changes. Nothing to do from here. Nice to have you with us.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Received 14 pages by fax from patient's previous primary care office, scanned to media.

Summary for chart (RN review):
- Cervical cytology 2023: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
- Childhood series complete per school record. HPV series completed in adolescence. Tdap given as an adult in 2021.
- No chronic problems listed. No medications. NKDA.
- Last visit there 2023, routine.
Next Pap due 2026.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came by after school for vaccines. No fever or illness today, no prior reactions. Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM to left arm; updated COVID vaccine 0.3 mL IM to right arm. VIS sheets reviewed. Observed 15 min, felt fine, left ambulatory.

documents.title: Immunization record request
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hello, the district HR office is updating staff files and asked me for proof of my shots, including the flu and COVID ones from the fall. Could someone send me a printout? Thank you!

documents.title: RE: Immunization record request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Sadie, your full immunization history, including what came over from your old office, is attached as a PDF. Let us know if HR needs it on a particular form.

documents.title: Car accident
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I was in a really bad car accident on Monday. My friend was in the car with me and she died. I only got banged up a little and I'm okay physically but I can't sleep, and when I do I wake up from dreams about it. I can't focus on anything. I don't know if this is something you see people for but I didn't know who else to ask.

documents.title: RE: Car accident
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sadie, I'm so sorry. That is a terrible thing to go through, and yes, this is exactly what we are here for. I'd like to see you in person. Can you come in Monday at 10:30? Reply here and I'll hold the slot. If at any point you feel unsafe or have thoughts of hurting yourself, call 988 or go to the nearest emergency room.

events.reason: sleep problems and nightmares after car crash

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: distress, insomnia and nightmares after a fatal car crash

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 27F seen a week after a serious crash on 7/21. A friend of hers was killed at the scene and Sadie saw it happen. Her own injuries were minor and she says they have mostly healed, nothing hurts now. Since then she lies awake for hours, wakes from nightmares about the crash, and cannot hold her attention on lesson planning or reading. Has not driven since. Her parents have been staying with her on and off. No prior counseling or psychiatric care. No alcohol or other substances, has not tried anything for sleep. Denies thoughts of harming herself.

O: vitals as charted, within normal range. Tired-appearing, tearful when describing the crash, otherwise appropriate and organized. Heart regular, lungs clear. No residual tenderness or bruising of note. Neuro nonfocal.

A: significant distress with insomnia, nightmares and poor concentration one week after a traumatic event in which she witnessed a death.

P: discussed that these reactions are common early on and that getting specialized help now matters. Urgent referral to psychiatry placed; front desk to call for the earliest opening. Sleep basics reviewed. She prefers to hold off on any medication until she has been evaluated. Crisis line and ED precautions reviewed. I'll check in after she is seen.

events.reason: psychiatric evaluation after motor vehicle collision

documents.title: Outpatient Psychiatry Consultation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient psychiatry consultation, visit of 08/04/2025. Thank you for the referral.

Ms. Nakamura is a 27-year-old teacher seen two weeks after a car crash in which she had minor injuries and witnessed the death of a friend. Since then she has had intrusive, upsetting memories of the event, steers clear of driving and of conversations about it, and describes feeling numb and cut off from the people around her. She is on guard much of the time and startles easily. These symptoms are getting in the way of her work preparations and her social life. No psychiatric history before this. No medications. Allergies: none known. Family history notable for maternal hypothyroidism and paternal hypertension. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Vital signs within normal limits. General physical examination unremarkable. Mental status: anxious, cooperative, linear thought process, no suicidal or homicidal ideation.

Impression: acute stress reaction.

Plan: referred to a trauma-focused therapist for weekly sessions. No medication at this time. Please obtain a CBC, TSH and urine drug screen before her return in about one month.

Outpatient psychiatry

documents.title: Lab draw
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Blood drawn from left antecubital on the first try, urine collected. Orders per the psychiatry consult letter: CBC, TSH, urine drug screen. Pt asked that results also go to her psychiatrist; fax number confirmed from the letter. Her mother drove her in today.

documents.title: Results from yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sadie, everything from yesterday is normal: blood counts and thyroid are fine and the urine screen was negative. We faxed a copy to psychiatry for your visit next week. Thinking of you, and glad you have started with the therapist.

documents.title: Follow-up and work forms
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I saw the psychiatrist again yesterday. Honestly not much better. I keep having flashbacks, I still barely sleep and I feel on edge all the time. I haven't driven since the accident and I haven't been able to go back to school, the kids started last week without me. She doesn't want to start any medicine right now and wants me to keep going to therapy every week, which I am. The district needs a leave form from a doctor. Can you fill it out? I'll drop it at the front desk.

documents.title: RE: Follow-up and work forms
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Of course. Drop it off whenever is easy and I'll get it done in a day or two. Please don't worry about the timing; healing from this takes time, and you are doing the right things.

documents.title: Leave of absence paperwork
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: School district leave of absence form completed and signed by PCP, faxed to district HR; confirmation page received. Original scanned to media. Pt notified by phone, copy left for her at the front desk.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for seasonal vaccines, her father drove her. Afebrile, feels well physically. Flu vaccine IM left deltoid, COVID 2025-26 formula IM right deltoid. Tolerated both, watched 15 minutes without problems. Said therapy is going, slowly.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency department record, date of service 01/17/2026.

28 yo woman, followed by outpatient psychiatry since August and September 2025 after a car crash last July. Comes in tonight because sleep has been poor again, she jumps at any loud noise, and she has felt removed from her surroundings, as if things around her are not quite real. Continues to avoid driving. Has not gone back to her teaching job. Takes no medications. NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Triage: BP 130/85, HR 98, RR 18, T 98.6 F.
Anxious-appearing, pulse fast. Otherwise exam without acute findings. Oriented, speech normal, no suicidal or homicidal ideation, no psychosis.
CBC and BMP within normal limits.

Impression: acute stress reaction following motor vehicle collision.
Disposition: discharged home with family. Follow up with her psychiatrist and primary care this week.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: f/u after ED Saturday night; their note came over Monday. Says the weeks around the holidays were harder, sleep slipped again, every slammed door makes her jump, and Saturday everything around her started to feel unreal, like a stage set, and she got scared, so her mom took her in. Labs there normal. Still seeing her therapist weekly. Still not driving and still on leave from school. No meds, no alcohol. Denies any thoughts of self-harm or wanting to be dead.

O: vitals as charted. Anxious, fidgeting, but engaged, good eye contact, thoughts organized. Heart regular, lungs clear. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P: acute stress reaction after the July crash, symptoms flaring.
- She will call psychiatry today to ask for an earlier appointment; I sent a note to her psychiatrist as well.
- Continue weekly therapy.
- She does not want medication; discussed that this can be revisited with psychiatry.
- 988 and ED precautions reviewed, mother aware.
- See me in a few months, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just an update: psychiatry got me in yesterday. We're sticking with therapy every week and no medicine for now. Thanks for reaching out to her.

documents.title: RE: Update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting us know, Sadie. Glad you were seen quickly. We'll plan on seeing you in May.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine check-in. Has not missed a week of therapy since August. Nightmares are less frequent than in the winter. Still not driving at all; her parents drive her to appointments and errands. Has not needed the ED again. No medications.

Vitals as charted, unremarkable. Calm, conversational, smiles easily today. Heart and lungs normal.

Acute stress reaction: gradually improving with therapy. Continue current care with psychiatry and her therapist. Due for her annual physical and Pap this fall; front desk to schedule.
